extracted.intended_audience: literate English readers (early-18th-century gentlemen and ladies; readers of The Spectator)
extracted.subtask_description: A set of short didactic essays offering advice on personal conduct, social advancement, civic virtue, and moral reflections drawn from anecdotes and fables for early-18th-century readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set forms of prayer to curb extravagant desires
rubrics_metrics.description: Among other Reasons for set Forms of Prayer, I have often thought it a very good one, that by this means the Folly and Extravagance of Mens Desires may be kept within due Bounds, and not break out in absurd and ridiculous Petitions on so great and solemn an Occasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Menippus fable illustrates the vanity of human wishes and secret devotions; prescribed/formal prayers help prevent ridiculous, excessive petitions to the divine. Use fixed forms to restrain folly in petitions and focus devotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Friends should be sincere 'mirrors' rather than flatterers
rubrics_metrics.description: If a sincere Friend were miraculously changed into a Looking-Glass, she should not be ashamed to ask its Advice very often. The Looking-Glass (Fidelio) relates that truth-telling, even when offensive, preserves integrity and usefulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A true monitor will reflect faults and truth (as the mirror that offended Narcissa by calling her ugly). Sincerity may offend but is more valuable than flattery; friends should advise candidly to improve the mind rather than merely adorn the body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convert natural pleasures into religious gratitude (moralize delight)
rubrics_metrics.description: I would have my Readers endeavour to moralize this natural Pleasure of the Soul, and to improve this vernal Delight ... into a Christian Virtue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When inspired by the beauties of spring and nature, use that temper of mind to practice gratitude and praise. The pleasure of observing creation is a fitting preparation for thanksgiving and devotion; cultivate habitually so that ordinary walks become acts of worship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use natural philosophy to deepen appreciation and rational admiration
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural Philosophy quickens this Taste of the Creation, and renders it not only pleasing to the Imagination, but to the Understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rest on mere sensory enjoyment; study the ends and providence evident in nature to elevate pleasure into rational admiration close to devotion. This heightens the mind's pleasure and leads to a more refined worship of the Creator.

rubrics_metrics.name: To gain influence, study and flatter what others most value
rubrics_metrics.description: You need no more than to discover what a Man values himself for; then of all things admire that Quality ... A Capacity for prostituting a Man's Self in his Behaviour, and descending to the present Humour of the Vulgar, is perhaps as good an Ingredient as any other for making a considerable Figure in the World.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical methods: observe people's particular vanities or pleasures and praise them; conform to the local humour (e.g., rustick cheerfulness in country life); engage in convivial practices valued by your audience (drinking, games). This adaptability carries social advancement, though it carries moral costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making court, presents and entertainments as means of advancement
rubrics_metrics.description: Next to this sort of Insinuation, which is called ... making one's Court, the most prevailing way is, by what better-bred People call a Present, the Vulgar a Bribe ... Generous Wines do every Day prevail, and that in great Points, where ten thousand times their Value would have been rejected with Indignation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific techniques cited: flattering under the guise of consulting, giving presents (or billets-doux understood at the bank), convivial distribution (citron-water, wines), and social compliance in leisure activities. The essay records these as effective but implicitly warns about their moral implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve integrity by making self-love the motive for justice
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Man has laid it down for a Position, that parting with his Integrity, in the minutest Circumstance, is losing so much of his very Self, Self-love will become a Virtue. By this means Good and Evil will be the only Objects of Dislike and Approbation; ... he that injures any Man, has effectually wounded the Man of this Turn as much as if the Harm had been to himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt the principle that protecting one's own integrity equates to protecting others; this artificial self-love secures impartiality and prevents corruption by emotional artifice (one may be misled into error but not guilt). The prescription is a moral strategy to resist bribery and flattery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware overconfidence after danger has passed (prudence over security)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing is more dangerous, than too much Confidence and Security ... The Trojans ... when they fancied the Siege was raised, and the Danger past, were the very next Night burnt in their Beds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain vigilance and moderation even after apparent safety; do not let relief or success breed reckless behaviour. The caution is applied especially to young women after May but is a general prudential rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modesty and chastity are the primary female virtues; beauty without innocence is worthless
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no Charm in the Female Sex, that can supply the place of Virtue. Without Innocence, Beauty is unlovely, and Quality contemptible, Good-breeding degenerates into Wantonness, and Wit into Impudence. ... it is observed, that all the Virtues are represented ... but if any one of them has a more particular Title to that Sex, it is Modesty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice to women: observe modesty especially after the dangers of spring; avoid perpetual 'May' dispositions; practice moderation in amusements (romances, chocolate) and preserve chastity as highest social and moral good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use time and restraint in courtship and sexual conduct (prudential calendaring)
rubrics_metrics.description: They may now reflect with Pleasure on the Dangers they have escaped ... I shall now allow my Fair Readers to return to their Romances and Chocolate, provided they make use of them with Moderation, till about the middle of the Month, when the Sun shall have made some Progress in the Crab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical seasonal/temporal guidance: young people should delay sexual engagement and exercise restraint for a period; cultural/astrological timing is used rhetorically to recommend measured behaviour rather than impulsive passion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punning: its origins, social function, and mixed value
rubrics_metrics.description: The Monopoly of Punns in this University has been an immemorial Privilege ... this humbler Exercise may be as instrumental in diverting us from any innovating Schemes and Hypothesis in Wit ... it fills the Imagination with an Assemblage of such Ideas and Pictures as are hardly any thing but Shade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Causes suggested: love-sickness, diet/atmosphere (kitchen fumes), melancholy. Effects/role: a harmless diversion that may keep people from dangerous speculative errors; yet it can be a sign of intellectual twilight and provokes divided opinions. The letter recommends toleration but offers critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities that justify esteem of a statesman or minister
rubrics_metrics.description: Candor and Openness of Heart, which shine in all your Words and Actions, exacts the highest Esteem ... a Secretary of State, in the Interests of Mankind, joined with that of his Fellow-Subjects, accomplished with a great Facility and Elegance in all the Modern as well as Ancient Languages, was a happy and proper Member of a Ministry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praised qualities: candor, openness, condescension, facility in modern and ancient languages, knowledge of books and men, and polite literature. These traits make a public servant effective and esteemed; the dedication uses them as standards of judgment for political character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize how small, frivolous behaviours create social access and power
rubrics_metrics.description: I have been considering the little and frivolous things which give Men Accesses to one another, and Power with each other ... saluting Rows of old Women, drinking with Clowns, and being upon a level with the lowest Part of Mankind in that wherein they themselves are lowest, their Diversions, will carry a Candidate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attention to minor social rituals (saluting, drinking, matching diversions) is a pragmatic criterion: mastery of these small behaviors can secure influence and office. The essay treats this as an explanatory rule of social mechanics, again with implied moral ambivalence.
